what: The three.js camera (fov 26) sits 280 inside the near edge of the ring (height 50, phones pull back 1750 more) looking at the opposite arc, and N cards (600×600 · corner 44, name strip 65px from the bottom) stand around a radius of 2800 facing inward, so the far cards on the opposite side look small in one concavely curved line. Each frame it auto-rotates .00035rad, dragging shifts the target by .0015rad per 1px, and the actual rotation follows by .05 per frame. While an arrow is held it turns ±.007rad per frame. Hovering a card brings it closer to 1.06x over .35s power2.out (.45s on release) and the name appears in the caption.

options.radius · fov: Ring radius · camera field of view, default 2800 · 26
options.auto · drag · cruise · follow: Auto-rotate speed (rad/Frame) · drag multiplier (rad/px) · arrow speed (rad/Frame) · follow share, defaults .00035 · .0015 · .007 · .05
options.[data-fx-part=stage]: Panel to hold the canvas (height via css) — if absent, the panel itself
options.[data-fx-part=card]: Card material (required) — the text becomes a name band, and --fx-card (background), --fx-rim (border) and color draw the placeholder image
options.[data-fx-part=prev] · [data-fx-part=next: (If present) Arrow that spins while pressed · name of the hovered card
options.inset · lift: Distance the camera comes in from the ring’s front edge · ring height, default 280 · 50

use: Concept 01…
note: The original scatters the hovered card image into pixel particles and gathers it back — the part does it only as a 1.06x approach (noted in the copy’s gaps). Touch accepts horizontal drag only, and vertical swipe is left to page scroll.
